comment: The FLIPPED row of the in-game gate: what a player who opened the Mod Settings screen and typed did. Every name here but one is a stock base 2.0 item, fluid or science pack, so the row loads on an install with no other mod. It is the COMPLEMENT of the mirror's stand-in table, field by field: quench-medium sits on the oil PRESET with a text the language REFUSES beside it, so the preset decides exactly as it would for a player who typed nothing, where the mirror leaves a dropdown deciding through an untouched text on the chain pair instead; chain-links sits on the long preset with a text that OVERRIDES it, carrying a fluid and a fractional amount, where the mirror leaves that text alone; and the research cost is overridden WHOLE here, count, time and pack text together, where the mirror moves one field and lets the military tier supply the other two. rivet-ingredients is the whole list of a recipe with no dropdown in front of it, taken as written, where the mirror puts a text the language refuses in the same field. tips-count is spelled whole and forging-time with a fraction, so the file carries the signed 64-bit encoding and the double encoding into the same engine run. tips-packs is THE TYPO: a science pack the game does not have, and quench-ingredients is its RECIPE twin, an item the game does not have typed into a text setting bound to a recipe's ingredient list. The two are one row on purpose: a refused text leaves BOTH channels deciding exactly as they would for a player who typed nothing, which in this row is the military tier's own packs and the oil preset's own ingredients rather than anything the mod declared, and the recipe channel is the one that carries the engine's 200-byte-per-element ceiling, since a recipe's note alone is 265 bytes for this setting name, 266 as the ELEMENT the engine measures with the newline that joins it onto the author's own description, and the whole disclosure used to stop the load. The quench recipe therefore comes out with the OIL preset's own ingredients, exactly as it would for a player who left the field alone, and its description carries the note in chunks the engine accepts. A refused player text no longer stops the load, so this row is what says so on a real engine: it must exit 0, price the research on the packs the MILITARY TIER carries, keep the quench recipe on the oil preset, and carry exactly two ERROR lines, one per refused text, each naming its own setting. Before that decision this file could hold no such text at all, because the run it produced was a failed load.
